candidate_visual_philosophy.statement: Build a complete brand world by assigning process, product, origin and dining context distinct semantic roles, then bind them through a forceful but disciplined information cadence.

candidate_stable_grammar.statement: A real process/action image owns the first read while retaining product and operator legibility.
At least three visibly distinct information roles prevent the work from collapsing into one headline and one product image.
Supporting modules each carry an origin, process, product or place meaning and form a directed campaign sequence.
Graphic marks are derived from ingredients, tools or place rather than selected as generic decoration.
A context layer shows the social or spatial world around the product, broadening the identity beyond a dish advertisement.

candidate_variation_axes.statement: The macro composition may move away from the reference's exact top/middle/bottom bands if semantic roles and reading order remain distinct.
Black/red/ivory intensity may shift while process heat, hierarchy and one coherent campaign identity survive.

candidate_compatibility_constraints.statement: Best suited to content with credible process, ingredient/origin and dining-context assets; a single isolated product image is insufficient.

unresolved_contradictions.question: Can the family remain recognizable without black/red/ivory and rough display lettering?
Can campaign module logic survive a substantially different aspect ratio and macro composition?
